stem: Rifampin is used with other medications to treat which serious infection?

options.label: A
options.misconception: Links rifampin to any bacterial pneumonia rather than to mycobacterial disease.
options.explanation: Mycoplasma pneumoniae lacks a cell wall and causes atypical pneumonia treated with a macrolide or doxycycline; rifampin is not used for it.

options.label: B
options.misconception: None — rifampin is part of combination TB therapy.
options.explanation: Rifampin is given with other medications to treat tuberculosis, a serious infection that affects the lungs and sometimes other parts of the body.

options.label: C
options.misconception: Confuses an antimycobacterial drug with an antifungal for invasive lung disease.
options.explanation: Invasive aspergillosis is a mold infection treated with voriconazole; rifampin acts on bacterial RNA polymerase and has no antifungal role.

options.label: D
options.misconception: Assumes a broad antimicrobial covers viral encephalitis.
options.explanation: Herpes simplex encephalitis is treated with intravenous acyclovir; rifampin is an antibacterial with no activity against herpesviruses.

options.label: E
options.misconception: Confuses antimycobacterial therapy with the penicillin used for syphilis.
options.explanation: Primary syphilis is Treponema pallidum infection treated with benzathine penicillin G; rifampin has no place in its treatment.

context: Learning objective: Rifampin is used with other medications to treat tuberculosis, which affects the lungs and sometimes other body sites.
